Question Choices: Put the fractions in order from largest to smallest 4/9, 4/7, 4/12
Hints: For the same whole or equal-sized wholes, a larger positive denominator means smaller pieces. Compare the same positive number of those pieces.
Solution: The numerator is 4 throughout. Sevenths are larger than ninths, which are larger than twelfths. Descending order: 4/7, 4/9, 4/12.

Question Choices: Select, Student A practiced for 1/4 of an hour and Student B for 4/16 of an hour. Who practiced longer time? ~~The-same | Student-A | Student-B~~
Solution: 4/16 simplifies to 1/4 by dividing both numbers by 4. Both practiced for 1/4 of an hour, or 60 divided by 4 = 15 minutes. Select The-same.

Question Choices: Each friend has a pizza of the same size. Emma ate 1/6 of her pizza, Liam ate 4/6 of his pizza, and Noah ate 2/6 of his pizza. Who ate the most pizza?
Hints: For the same whole or equal-sized wholes, equal denominators mean equal-sized pieces. Compare the numerators.
Solution: The pizzas are equal-sized and all portions count sixths. Since 4 > 2 > 1, Liam ate the most, 4/6 of a pizza.

Question Choices: Select. Can 3/8 of a short road be longer than 1/8 of a long road? ~~Yes | No~~
Solution: Yes. Take a short road of 8 kilometres and a long road of 16 kilometres. Three eighths of 8 is 3 kilometres; one eighth of 16 is 2 kilometres. Here 3/8 of the short road is longer.

Question Choices: Select, Which is larger 1/2 of a smaller cake or 1/4 of a larger cake? ~~1/2-smaller-cake | 1/4-larger-cake | Cannot-tell~~
Hints: Do we know the exact sizes?
Solution: Cannot-tell. If the cakes weigh 8 and 12 units, half the smaller cake weighs 4, while a quarter of the larger weighs 3. If the cakes weigh 8 and 20 units, the portions weigh 4 and 5. The result changes with the whole sizes.
